correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the b-coloring definition directly. In a complete multipartite graph, any color is confined to one part. If a part uses at least two colors, every vertex in that part misses another in-part color from its closed neighborhood, so none of those color classes has a color-dominating vertex. Therefore all parts are monochromatic and have distinct colors, forcing exactly r colors; then every vertex is color-dominating. Sorting reduces realizability to the coordinatewise inequalities. The labeled counting formula follows because at step i exactly c_i-(i-1) eligible unused parts remain. The finite verifier checks the definition independently on 16 small complete multipartite graphs, 7200 surjective proper colorings, 144 b-colorings, and 189 sequence instances.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification on a canonical graph family, not an arbitrary finite slice. It determines the entire realized-sequence poset, S-spectrum behavior, unique maximal realized sequence, and exact labeled-coloring count. The maximal sequence recovers the multipartite part-size partition, so the new invariant captures strictly finer structural information than the ordinary b-chromatic number on this family. Complete multipartite graphs are also the base objects in distance-to-co-cluster parameterizations, giving the result a natural role as a benchmark for future sequence-b-coloring algorithms.
